What the emulator learns—and what still blocks diagnostic assimilation

A short, physics-first summary of completed 85604 evidence. No 85606 result appears here.

old 85604 onlyfive reduced fieldstransport evaluated from fields, not used as a loss

Short answer

Mean dynamics improved. Joint transport uncertainty did not.

Forecast: repeated short steps retain turbulent structure and transport timing better than large direct jumps.

Uncertainty: the ensemble gets local transport spread roughly right, but distant patches cancel too strongly. Total transport spread is only about half of what the errors require.

Sparse measurements: two local density views contain real information about a separate unseen region, mainly at low and middle toroidal modes.

01 · Forecasted structure

Small rollout steps retain structure; long jumps smooth it away

At the same 25.055-microsecond horizon, eight one-frame steps keep much more of the pressure and potential pattern than two four-frame steps or one direct jump.

02 · Mean transport

The short-step rollout follows transport timing best

Each point below is a separate rolling-origin forecast. The one-frame rollout tracks many rises and falls; the longer direct forecasts collapse toward a smooth, low-amplitude trace.

03 · Why the ensemble still fails

Correct local spread does not imply correct total transport spread

Spread-skill ratio compares forecast spread with actual error; 1 is ideal. Local values are near 1. Integrated values are 0.41–0.49 because distant fluctuations cancel incorrectly. Simply inflating every member enough to fix the total would make local uncertainty more than twice too large.

04 · Model ladder

Each model tested one specific explanation

ModelAssumption testedWhat happened
Compressed latent diffusionA small latent state retains the physics needed for future frames.It produced plausible fields, but rollout structure and transport decayed. A larger latent recovered fine reconstruction detail without repairing dynamics or assimilation.
Codec-free deterministic operatorThe visible five-field transition is mostly predictable, and compression is the bottleneck.Direct field prediction improved short-horizon structure and mean transport. Repeated short steps beat large jumps physically. It cannot represent forecast uncertainty.
Joint residual diffusionUnpredictable error can be learned as one joint distribution around the deterministic mean.It improved local spread and spectra. It missed how distant transport patches fluctuate together, so integrated spread stayed near 0.4–0.5 of the required value.
Deep state-conditioned diffusionThe residual distribution changes with the current plasma state.Conditioning improved marginal scores and was the strongest earlier stochastic baseline, but it still did not recover domain-scale transport covariance.
Toroidally equivariant, multiscale diffusionTranslation symmetry and noise at several spatial scales are the missing ingredients.Symmetry became cleaner, but more structure did not monotonically improve transport. Noise at several resolutions was not the same as one coherent global plasma state.
Persistent global–local generatorA latent state shared across space and four future frames can coordinate the ensemble.Its mean forecast improved spectra, density–potential phase, and mean transport. Its stochastic branch remained too weak: integrated spread-skill fell to about 0.22.
Full evolved-state operator pilotMissing Hermes variables, rather than stochastic modeling, are the main bottleneck.The pilot overfit: training improved while chronological validation stayed near the zero-increment baseline. This hypothesis remains plausible but unproven.

05 · Sparse simultaneous measurements

Two local density views predict part of an unseen region

This is spatial reconstruction, not forecasting. Measurements A and B are revealed at one instant; region C is hidden and predicted.

Bottom line

What is safe to present

SupportedNot supported yet
Short-step deterministic rollouts preserve structure and mean transport better than long direct jumps.No current ensemble has passed the integrated transport-covariance gate.
The uncertainty failure is spatial coordination, not simply too little scalar noise.Earlier ETKF diagnostic rankings are exploratory until the prior covariance improves.
Two sparse simultaneous density measurements recover useful nonlocal low/mid-mode information.The synthetic boxes are not full experimental diagnostic models, and this is not cross-shot validation.
